title: Quant precision investigation - scratchpad
content:
Context:
- Investigating intermittent NaNs and sudden quality regressions when serving Llama-like 13B family with mixed precision quantized backends (INT8 and experimental FP8 pathways). Issue seen only on dedicated cluster (A100s) but sometimes reproducible locally on dev RTX 6000.
- Symptoms: model outputs contain literal "nan" tokens or generation halts with RuntimeError: CUDA kernel returned NaN; softmax produces NaN logits; occasional loss spike during evaluation.

What I observed (chronological breadcrumbs):
- 2026-02-25 09:12: first customer report: short hallucination bursts + occasional "[NaN]" in text.
- 2026-02-26 14:00: reproduced locally with quantized artifact v2-int8-converted. Loss curve on evaluation set jumps at step ~32.
- 2026-02-27 10:30: tried bnb conversion with --force-bnb-quant; small improvement but still NaN in ~1/2000 generations.
- 2026-03-01 17:05: switched to per-channel quantization for weights (instead of per-tensor) — huge reduction in q-error for some layers but NaN persists.
- 2026-03-05 11:48: enabling fp32 attention fallback (manual patch in serving runtime) removed NaNs entirely but latency increased ~12% — strong indication attention kernels cause instability.

Commands and snippets I ran: (copy-paste style)
- Convert (bitsandbytes):
  python convert_model.py --model-dir /mnt/models/llama13b-ft --out /tmp/llama13b-int8 --quantize 8 --per_channel
  >>> conv finished, warnings: layer 43 - high MSE

- Quick reproduce (eval script):
  PYTORCH_JIT=0 CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 python eval_gen.py --model /tmp/llama13b-int8 --prompt-file prompts.txt --max-tokens 256
  >>> RuntimeError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered (when running attention_forward)

- Debug run (with float fallback):
  export REDWOOD_FORCE_ATTENTION_FP32=1
  python serve_local.py --model /tmp/llama13b-int8 --port 8080
  >>> generation stable; no NaNs.

Error snippets captured:
- stack trace (trimmed):
  File "/opt/serve/attention_kernels.cpp", line 214, in compute_attn
  CUDA kernel returned NaN at 0x7f12c3

- model output example:
  "The patient was stable. nan nan nan. Further tests are recommended."

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Attention kernel numerical instability when using fused int8 / fp8 kernels + KV cache reuse. Overflow or denormals causing NaNs.
2) Incorrect quant scale/zero_point metadata on per-channel weights (conversion bug) leading to extreme dequantized magnitudes in a few heads.
3) Uninitialized scratch memory in custom fused kernels (race condition) that manifests only with particular batch/seq combos.
4) Backcompat bug: serving runtime attempts to reuse an FP16 cache buffer as BF16/FP8 buffer (dtype aliasing) causing bit-level nonsense.
5) Calibration dataset missing edge-case tokens -> calibration produces too-small scales and causes underflow to denormals -> unstable ops.

Quick checks I performed and results:
- Histogram of dequantized weights for suspect layers -> heavy tail on layer 43 and 44; max magnitude 5x expected. Suggests bad scale for that per-channel group.
- Re-run conversion with synthetic calibration (uniform random) -> reduces extremes; produced fewer NaNs but not eliminated.
- torch.autograd.detect_anomaly didn't trigger earlier because error occurs inside custom CUDA kernel (no autograd info).
- Running with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 gives slightly better stack traces but still hard to pinpoint because kernel only sometimes returns NaN.
- Running with TF32 disabled/CUDNN deterministic flags had no impact.

Immediate mitigations tried in prod branch: (short experiments)
- Add guarded clamp after dequantize: torch.clamp(deq, -1e3, 1e3) -> eliminated NaN in one long run but felt hacky and masks root cause.
- Fall back to BF16-only attention kernels when serving for tier B customers -> fixes but increases cost.
- Re-convert model using per-channel symmetric quant and min-max clipping (clip at 99.999th percentile) -> fewer NaNs, but some prompts still problematic.

Ideas for deeper debugging (next steps):
- Build minimal repro that triggers NaN in pure inference loop (no networking). Start with batch size 1 and gradually increase seq length until failure. Record exact input tokens.
- Instrument kernel to write debug sentinel on first NaN detection (index, head, layer, seq pos) to persistent log (fast path, low overhead).
- Add unit test coverage for conversion script: deliberately corrupt scale metadata to assert converter throws.
- Re-run conversion under valgrind-like memory check for CUDA (cuda-memcheck) to search for out-of-bounds writes: cuda-memcheck --tool memcheck python convert_model.py ...
- Add reproducible random seeds across conversion + eval to rule out nondeterminism at conversion-time.
- Compare per-channel scales between bitsandbytes conversion and our internal converter; diff expected vs actual per-channel scale arrays.
- Use fp32 run to get golden logits for the failing prompt, then compare intermediate dequantized activations layer-by-layer to detect where divergence explodes.

Notes on tooling and flags to try: (practical)
- CUDA: cuda-memcheck, Nsight Systems, nvprof (though deprecated), and cuda-gdb for local debug.
- PyTorch: TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA=1 (if compiled) to catch out-of-bounds; set torch.set_printoptions(edgeitems=20) to dump tensors selectively.
- Environment toggles we used: REDWOOD_FORCE_ATTENTION_FP32, REDWOOD_QUANT_CLAMP (experimental), BNB_EXT_DEBUG=1.
- Runtime compile flags: build fused kernels with -march=native vs safe numeric flags. Try disabling fused kernels to narrow down.

Action items (TODOs):
- [ ] Create minimal failing input and attach to ticket INF-2045 (owner: Maya) due 2026-03-14.
- [ ] Add assertive checks in converter to validate per-channel scales are finite and > eps. (owner: Owen) due 2026-03-12.
- [ ] Add redwood option to force attention float fallback per-model; add rollout flag to console. (owner: Priya) backlog.
- [ ] Instrument fused attention kernel to log first NaN coords with low overhead. (owner: eng-serving-runtime) sprint 18.
- [ ] Compare dequantized activations vs fp32 golden for failing prompt; build small diff tool. (owner: Maya/Owen) due 2026-03-16.

Loose thoughts / brainstorming (notes to self):
- Could be cross-talk between KV cache dtype conversions and attention softmax (softmax on large negative numbers -> underflow -> zeros then division by zero?). Maybe intermediate exponent overflow/underflow path produces NaN.
- If scale is zero for a channel (bad metadata), dequantize divides by zero -> nan. Add guard for scale <= tiny.
- Consider adding small per-channel epsilon to scale stored in model metadata on convert.

Reference links / quick pointers:
- GH PR: github:repo/conv-quant#PR-1287 (contains conversion change I merged on 2026-02-24)
- Ticket: jira:INF-2045 (NaN in production for quant models)
- Slack thread: slack:#infra-quant-debug (runtime traces and short clips)

End of scratchpad - keep iterating.

Maya
2026-03-11
